messages:
matt: heads up — running into a weird retry loop on Android when our Kotlin SDK uses Retrofit + OkHttp. Flow: call returns 401, authenticator attempts refresh, interceptor adds new header, but the call keeps retrying 401 repeatedly on a background worker. Any quick guesses?

kevin: @matt can you paste the okhttp config + whether you use application vs network interceptors? also which okhttp version? :eyes:

matt: okhttp 4.11.0, Retrofit 2.9, here's a minimal reproduction in our sample app:
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .authenticator(TokenAuthenticator()) // calls refreshToken synchronously
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor()) // adds Authorization header from token provider
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .build()

val retrofit = Retrofit.Builder()
  .baseUrl("https://api.redwood.example/")
  .client(client)
  .build()
```
When the token is expired the first 401 triggers TokenAuthenticator which does a blocking network refresh. The refresh succeeds, but we see 3-4 immediate retries and then the whole workitem fails with a timeout.

maria: hmmm sounds like interceptor ordering + okhttp's RetryAndFollowUpInterceptor behavior. If your AuthInterceptor is an application interceptor it won't see the header added by the authenticator on the follow-up request. You should use addNetworkInterceptor for header mutation that must be present on retried requests.

matt: interesting — we added the header in the application interceptor because we needed to read from a local token store. switching to network interceptor is tricky because we want to avoid hitting disk on the network thread.

kevin: another angle: authenticators are called only for responses with code 401/407 by okhttp internal retry logic. If your TokenAuthenticator performs another Retrofit call that itself uses the same OkHttpClient, you can get reentrancy and weird retry loops. Classic: authenticator calls token endpoint -> gets 401 -> authenticator invoked again -> infinite loop.

sophia: yes that's the reentrancy bug. Solution patterns we used elsewhere:
- Make token refresh call with a dedicated OkHttpClient that has no authenticator and no interceptors, or
- Have TokenAuthenticator use a synchronous HTTP client (okhttp newClientWithoutAuth) or HTTPUrlConnection for the refresh, or
- Use a short-circuit in the authenticator to detect requests to the token endpoint and return null to avoid recursion.

maria: also consider disabling retryOnConnectionFailure for auth-sensitive calls and set a call timeout so the worker doesn't hang forever. Example safe config:
```kotlin
val refreshClient = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(false)
  .callTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .build()

class TokenAuthenticator: Authenticator {
  override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? {
    if (response.request.url.encodedPath.contains("/token")) return null // avoid recursion
    val newToken = runBlocking { refreshTokenWith(refreshClient) } // synchronous but bounded
    return response.request.newBuilder()
      .header("Authorization", "Bearer $newToken")
      .build()
  }
}
```

matt: that makes sense. Quick follow-up — any Android-specific quirks (proguard, okhttp threads, retrofit call adapters) we should watch for?

kevin: proguard rarely affects okhttp runtime behavior unless you obfuscate reflection used by a custom call adapter. More common: Retrofit's default CallAdapter (synchronous vs coroutine) and how you cancel/timeout. If you're running in WorkManager and a worker gets stopped, cancellations can leave things half-done. Ensure you use callTimeout and also cancel the Call on worker shutdown.

sophia: also note okhttp 5 changed interceptor ordering semantics slightly. Our SDK should document the recommended pattern and ship a helper factory: "makeAuthRefreshClient" that configures a separate refresh client. Right now the Kotlin SDK examples only show attaching an authenticator directly which invites this bug.

matt: are we able to change the SDK default quickly? I'd like to avoid every Android app hitting this footgun.

maria: proposal: expose a boolean flag in the SDK config `useDedicatedRefreshClient` (default true for Android), and update samples to show `addNetworkInterceptor` for header injection or use an in-memory token cache to avoid disk on network thread. Also add a note in the README about token endpoint recursion.

dev-ci-bot: deployment pipeline: created MR #4287 updating android SDK samples and adding a TokenAuthenticator pattern doc (link: https://git.internal/redwood/mr/4287) :shipit:

kevin: can someone file a short GH issue to track changing the default samples + add a test that simulates token endpoint 401 recursion? I'll pick it up if nobody objects.

matt: I'll open the issue and attach the sample app reproducer. Thanks for the quick triage everyone :heart:

sophia: thanks — added a checklist to the MR: update samples, add note on interceptor vs network-interceptor, include dedicated refresh client, and add a CI test using MockWebServer.
